results.response:

VFB records show 22 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types. The target-to-source weight is 7620 and the source-to-target weight is 2697.

VFB has annotated [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes for mushroom body output neurons and [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100248,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for KCab") downstream connectivity classes for alpha/beta Kenyon cells, as well as [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes for mushroom body output neurons. 

To identify which specific mushroom body output neurons receive input from both alpha/beta and gamma Kenyon cells, you can query the downstream connectivity classes for these cell types. VFB holds data on the downstream targets of alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells, including 13 shared downstream target classes. 

Follow-up queries can be used to explore the specific connectivity patterns between alpha/beta Kenyon cells, gamma Kenyon cells, and mushroom body output neurons, such as listing the downstream connectivity classes for these cell types or examining the expression patterns overlapping with gamma Kenyon cells.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The containment hierarchy from the [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") up to the top-level brain structure is: antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum, as indicated by VFB. Alternatively, a longer chain is also recorded in VFB: antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. 

VFB holds various data related to the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, including [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records of Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, 10 records of Neurons with synaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, and [911](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records of Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1. 

To further explore the hierarchy and related data, you can query VFB for more information on the adult antennal lobe, adult deutocerebrum, adult cerebrum, adult central brain, and adult brain, as well as the neurons and images associated with these structures.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as noted by Thomas and Wyman (1984). VFB records show that there is one of these cells per hemisphere, with its large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, according to Koto et al. (1981). 

VFB holds [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") records of images of the Drosophila DNp01 giant fiber neuron, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, [361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records of downstream connectivity classes for DNp01, and [435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records of upstream connectivity classes for DNp01. The connectome data indicates that the Drosophila DNp01 giant fiber neuron has specific expression patterns and is mentioned in a publication about the Drosophila connectome.

VFB returned 10 genetic tool/expression pattern rows for the giant fiber neuron, including the P{VT046265-GAL4} expression pattern, and records the Drosophila DNp01 giant fiber neuron as having a GAL4 driver and expression pattern. 

The giant fiber neuron's connectivity can be described by its downstream and upstream connectivity classes. The downstream connectivity classes for DNp01, which are recorded in VFB, may indicate the neuron's postsynaptic partners, while the upstream connectivity classes for DNp01 may indicate the neuron's presynaptic partners. 

For more information, follow-up queries can be made to explore the available images, transgene expression, and connectivity classes of the giant fiber neuron.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response: The connectome data indicates that neuron types such as [ML-VPN2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052139 "Open ML-VPN2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052141 "Open Mt-VPN1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052140 "Open Mt-VPN in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mti](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052142 "Open Mti in Virtual Fly Brain"), and T4ai might mediate a connection between the [visual system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB records show that neuron types with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, such as [LoVC14](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20011421 "Open LoVC14 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [LoVC20](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20011423 "Open LoVC20 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [LoVC21](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20011424 "Open LoVC21 in Virtual Fly Brain"), could also mediate this connection. Furthermore, VFB holds data on adult visual projection neurons, which are predicted as mediating the connection between the visual system and the mushroom body, with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. VFB has annotated a large number of neurons with some part in the visual system ([1046](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047735,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in visual system")) and neurons with some part in the mushroom body ([602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body")), as well as neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body ([367](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body")), suggesting that visual information could reach the memory circuit via these connections. To further explore this, you can query VFB for specific neuron types and their connections to the visual system and mushroom body.

results.title: Comparative analysis
results.question: Compare the downstream targets of the two main types of clock neurons (s-LNv and l-LNv). Do they converge on any common target neuron types?
results.response:
The downstream targets of the two main types of clock neurons, [s-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch03yp "Open s-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain") and [l-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fws "Open l-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain"), have been compared. VFB records show that there are shared downstream target classes among these compared source classes. Specifically, VFB found 17 shared downstream target classes, including adult interneuron, adult cholinergic neuron, adult GABAergic neuron, adult glutamatergic neuron, adult octopaminergic neuron, adult dopaminergic neuron, and adult serotonergic neuron. 

These shared targets suggest that the s-LNv and l-LNv clock neurons may converge on common target neuron types, such as adult cholinergic neuron, adult octopaminergic neuron, and adult serotonergic neuron. Other shared target classes include neuron, adult neuron, adult CNS neuron, CNS neuron, sensory system neuron, and visual system neuron.

VFB holds these records on the compared downstream targets of s-LNv and l-LNv, providing evidence of potential convergence on common target neuron types. To further investigate the connectivity between these clock neurons and their downstream targets, you can explore the available data on VFB.

results.response:
The [subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051068 "Open subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") is a region in the Drosophila brain that has been characterised in VFB to some extent. In terms of connectomics data, VFB found 95 upstream class-connectivity partners for [larval subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051067 "Open larval subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") vine neuron. 

For genetic tools, VFB returned 4205 genetic tool/expression pattern rows for the subesophageal zone, including GAL4 drivers and binary/intersectional drivers. This suggests that there are various genetic tools available for studying SEZ neurons.

It is worth noting that the subesophageal zone is defined in VFB as a neuropil mass below the esophagus encompassing the three gnathal neuromeres and any regions of the cephalic (supraesophageal) neuromeres situated below the esophagus. 

To further explore the subesophageal zone, you can query VFB for more specific information on neuron types, connectomics data, and genetic tools.
